TWO READINGS FIT AND IMPLY OPPOSITE FIXES: (a) bte (134.2M, 80% of rs_even) is pathologically slow per element, or (b) there is a large FIXED cost per collective call and the five small 4.2M tables are the expense. val_bpb: fold log(g) into the exp bias; delete deriv by reusing a = dzc*th
column10: Both are algebraically exact in real arithmetic and look fine in float64 (abs diff ~7e-10 on a 4e5 scale), but AT FP32 - the precision the kernel runs in - dz differs by up to 8.29e-03 RELATIVE on saturated elements. Reason: dzf = pr - (pr*th)*th subtracts two numbers of magnitude |pr|, so its absolute error is |pr|*eps, while the current 1 - th*th subtracts two O(1) numbers. The agent asserted the cancellation is 'identical in both forms, so no new precision risk' - IT IS NOT, and only the fp32 check showed it. Folding log(g) into the bias alone gives dzc max rel 5.4e-06 (log+exp rounding) and leaves masked (g==0) rows at ~1e-40 instead of exactly 0 (harmless: underflows in fp32, contributes nothing through the matmul). Payoff is 2 full-width passes = 0.268e9 element-passes ~ 0.47% at the BEST rate ever measured on this file and ~0.1-0.25% after the standing 2-4x haircut - too small to justify a gate for a NON-EXACT change. LESSON: verify proposed kernel algebra at the KERNEL's precision, not just in float64; float64 hid a 0.8% fp32 error completely.

description: train3_s17.py + SWA=256 (vendor native sliding_window on BOTH attention calls)
val_bpb: does the vendor's compile-time tile skipping pay at 1024 context?
column10: fwd_bwd 0.369 vs 0.377 and 649 steps vs 646 = NO speed gain, AND bpb 1.116245 vs 1.105476 = +0.0108 WORSE. The vendor kernel genuinely does skip (tile_required is a COMPILE-TIME list, attention_bwd.py:890, not a mask - verified by reading it), but its key tiles are far coarser than the 128 I assumed, so at seqlen 1024 a 256 window has almost nothing to skip. Meanwhile applying a 256 window to ALL layers costs 15x the +0.0007 that the old odd-layers-only MASK test measured. The web research warned this exactly: sliding window's rationale is amortising quadratic cost at 16-64K context and 'likely NOT transferring' at 1024. It was right. Vendor attention_bwd (101.53 ms, 21% of the step) therefore has NO external lever: no tile-size parameter in its signature, sliding_window does not help at this context, and our own attention backward measured SLOWER than the vendor twice (ATTNBWD, ATTNBWD_V2).

description: train3_s18.py, ROPE_WIDE off vs on (paired, same file)

column10: fwd_bwd 0.373 -> 0.371, total 0.482 -> 0.482, steps 646 -> 646. ROPE_WIDE rotates the whole (128,512) q/k tile in three wide passes using host tables that carry the sin sign and exactly 1.0/0.0 on the ROPE_FRAC-truncated columns, replacing ~48 narrow 32-lane ops per head per tile in BOTH live _ko kernels. It deletes 176,640 of the 461,449 VectorE instructions (38%) and 5,760 DMA instructions, and removes the per-layer cos.repeat(b,1) (24x/step on a 4 MB tensor). Verified bit-identical in the NKI SIMULATOR (fwd and bwd) and independently by me in fp32 numpy (zero differing words). RESULT: ~11 ns recovered per deleted instruction, not the documented 104 ns and certainly not the 360 ns/instr the profile average implied. THE INSTRUCTION-COUNT PROGRAM IS DEAD.

val_bpb: what actually sets the step?
column10: No engine is the bottleneck: vector 69% active, tensor 49%, scalar 48%, dma 40% - nothing saturated - and removing 38% of the work on the BUSIEST engine changed the wall by 0.4%. The step is LATENCY-BOUND on the dependency chain through the graph, not throughput-bound on any unit. My error: I read per-instruction DURATION from the profile (374 ns vs ~267 ns of element time) as fixed overhead that gates the wall. Instruction duration is not critical-path time. This also retro-explains every other null today - bf16 gradients, back-to-back collectives, the collapsed scalar AdamW, and this - they were all THROUGHPUT optimisations on a LATENCY-bound machine. Consistent with the oldest note in the project memory ('Sep 10 profile: graphs latency-bound, all engines 30-60%'), which I rediscovered the expensive way. The only lever that remains consistent with this diagnosis is FEWER, LARGER KERNELS (shorter dependency chain), which this file has already been through (LAYER=op fused layers, PRE_BWD=fused); what is left is the VENDOR attention backward (101.5 ms, 21%) and the graph's serial structure.

description: submit/train.py (v52, EXACT submitted file) with /tmp/neff_cache MOVED ASIDE
val_bpb: true cold-compile timing after the portal returned States.Timeout
column10: PORTAL: sub-83850d03, v52, FAILED, States.Timeout, no val_bpb. Local TRUE cold run (cache emptied - every earlier 'cold compile ~430 s' in this ledger was WARM, the box holds 9,500 NEFFs): launch 00:06:07 -> finish 00:18:15 = 728 s for a 120 s training budget. Breakdown: init ~36 s | step-0 compile 503.6 s | training 120 s | eval 27.9 s | causality+save ~40 s. startup_allowance_est 541.6 s (UNDER the 900 s cap), over_budget False, causality passed. Cold compile produces 172 NEFFs / 78 MB, dominated by TWO graphs: 36.2 MB forward + 30.2 MB backward. FIXED OVERHEAD = 608 s, so a real 1800 s run here totals ~2408 s = 40.1 min. THE RISK: our train.py correctly back-dates over-cap compile against the budget (budget_started = now - excess, train.py:3702), so once compile exceeds 900 s the TOTAL WALL PINS AT ~2670 s + eval ~ 45.5 min regardless of how slow the compile is. At portal compile speed 1x -> 40.1 min, 2x -> 45.0, 3x -> 45.6. If the harness allows 45 min, a compile host ~2x slower than ours flips v52 from inside to outside, while v43 (16 kernels vs 21, smaller graphs) stays inside - which matches the evidence exactly (v43 scored, v52 timed out, nothing else about the run differs). NOT YET CONFIRMED: the portal's wall limit and machine are unknown, and a transient infrastructure timeout is still possible.

The compiler help says -O1 'aims to minimize compile-time' and the default is -O2, but compile here is dominated by the NKI kernels and graph partitioning, not by optimisation passes, so the knob does nothing. (Consistent with T17b from 2026-09-06, which found -O1 and -O2 identical in step time and loss.) --cache_dir is NOT a valid neuronx-cc argument on this version (NCC_EARG002); to force a cold compile, move /tmp/neff_cache aside instead.

val_bpb: does compile growth explain v52's portal States.Timeout?
column10: v43 cold step-0 compile = 602.98 s vs v52's 503.59 s. THE VERSION THAT SCORED COMPILES ~100 s SLOWER THAN THE ONE THAT TIMED OUT, despite v43 having 16 @nki.jit kernels to v52's 21. So compile time is NOT the differentiator and falling back to an earlier version would be strictly WORSE on both axes (slower compile AND +0.0074 bpb). It also bounds the portal: if its compile host were ~2x slower than ours, v43 (1206 s) would have overrun the 900 s allowance harder than v52 (1007 s) and timed out too - it did not. So the portal's compile speed and wall limit are comfortable for BOTH versions. REMAINING CANDIDATES for States.Timeout, in order: (1) transient portal infrastructure - now the leading hypothesis by elimination, and the reason to resubmit v52 UNCHANGED before changing anything; (2) the known intermittent sidecar/DGE fault (NRT Execution error, operation=nki_kernel_global, seen in G_WG and in four OOB crashes on the indirect-DMA embedding path) manifesting as a HANG rather than a crash, which would produce exactly this status. Note v52 runs correctly end to end cold here: allowance 541.6 s, over_budget False, causality passed, ~40 min projected total for a real 1800 s run.

val_bpb: both States.Timeout at ~1 hour
column10: Two identical failures rule out a transient. EXCLUDED BY MEASUREMENT: compile growth (v43, which scored, compiles SLOWER: 603 vs 504 s); compile contention (1 rank = 8 ranks); optlevel (-O1 = -O2); the scoring path (156 s of a 1200 s budget); --compile-only support (v52 implements it, train.py:3526); and our own budget accounting (over_budget False, back-dating correct at train.py:3702). REMAINING and UNOBSERVABLE from here: the harness's own phases (staging, the separate compile-only pass, container start) plus our ~2400 s process, against a limit that appears to be ~3600 s. v54 = v52 + (a) no in-run eval (-156 s, zero score cost) + (b) an adaptive total-wall guard (WALL_CAP_SECONDS=2700) that trades training steps for finishing ONLY when the run is late - dormant on this box, so the score is unchanged.

val_bpb: response to two systematic States.Timeout failures: an adaptive total-wall guard
column10: THE PROBLEM IT FIXES: training runs its full max_train_seconds measured from the 5th STEP BOUNDARY, so a slow compile does not shorten training - it pushes the whole run later until a harness wall limit kills it and we score NOTHING. WALL_CAP_SECONDS (default 2900) bounds wall since _PROCESS_STARTED, holding back WALL_RESERVE_SECONDS=300 for the checkpoint save (~820 MB), causality check, eval (156 s cold) and teardown. It rides the EXISTING stop-decision all_reduce (train.py control tensor, ReduceOp.MAX) so every rank still breaks on the same step. On this box training ends at ~2230-2346 s of wall and the guard triggers only above 2600 s, so it is DORMANT and the score is unchanged. On a host ~250 s slower to compile it starts trading training steps for finishing - strictly better than a timeout that returns nothing. NO model or kernel change; check_submission passes.

vehicle: v54 DECISION not to disable the in-run eval
val_bpb: why the obvious 156 s saving was rejected
column10: Turning --eval-public off would remove a second large graph compile (156 s cold, measured by running prepare.py eval-public standalone) from the scored run, and the portal appears to score independently via load_for_eval. REJECTED because we do NOT know whether the portal reads val_bpb from our stdout or computes it itself - the failed submission showed 'val_bpb -', which is consistent with either. If it reads ours, disabling the eval turns a SUCCESSFUL run into an unscorable one, which is far worse than 156 s of wall against a ~1200 s gap. Also note it is causality_check, not evaluate_bpb, that triggers the eval-shape compile, so skipping only the eval would have saved ~28 s, not 156 s. description: trn2_profile_one.sh capture + per-engine EXCLUSIVE-time sweep over start_ts/end_ts
val_bpb: why ROPE_WIDE paid 0 while MLP_WG_GROUP paid 5.6%
column10: For one fwd+bwd span of 199.9 ms: engine BUSY = Vector 139.7 / Tensor 99.0 / Scalar 97.0 / GpSimd 38.5 / Sync 26.8 ms, but engine EXCLUSIVE (the only engine working, i.e. where deleting work shortens the WALL) = Vector 27-31 / Tensor 15-36 / Scalar 12-15 ms. Concurrency: 1 engine 29.2%, 2 engines 40.5%, 3+ 28.0%, idle 2.4% - THE STEP IS ~70% OVERLAPPED. That is the whole explanation: Vector is busy 70% of the span but ALONE for only ~14%, so deleting vector work pays ONLY if it lands in that window. ROPE_WIDE deleted 38% of vector instructions from the OVERLAPPED regions -> exactly 0. MLP_WG_GROUP hit exclusive stretches -> -5.6%. METHOD TO REUSE: sweep-line the merged per-engine busy intervals, keep the stretches where exactly one engine is active, then attribute each instruction's overlap with its own engine's exclusive windows to its nki_source_location. Scripts kept at experimental/critpath.py and experimental/excl_attrib.py.

description: train3_s19.py + WVIEWS=1 (one differentiable torch.unbind per weight stack per forward)
val_bpb: fix the top exclusive-time item: 72 per-layer select_backwards
column10: fwd_bwd 0.356 vs 0.367-0.371 same-session, total 0.461 vs 0.475-0.476, 674 steps vs 651 = +3.5%, matching the 16.6 ms of vector-exclusive time the profile attributed to ONE line (53% of all vector-exclusive time). CAUSE: autograd lowers each of the 6x12=72 per-layer stack-slice selects as select_backward = zeros_like(the WHOLE stack) + scatter + a full-stack add; measured 15,506 MEMSET instrs x (128,512) = 1.016e9 elements vs 1.057e9 predicted from the stack shapes (4% agreement). BIT-IDENTICAL: layer i's slice touches a DISJOINT part of the stack, so torch.stack of the 12 grads is exactly the tensor the 12 scatter-adds produce, and the cast is elementwise - only the step count changes. This REFUTES the _StackSliceLinear docstring claim that the select-backward allocation is one 'which compile fuses away' - the profile shows it inside the compiled graph, on the critical path. val_bpb: where is the remaining exclusive time, and is the vendor attention backward worth attacking?
column10: Span 199.9 -> 181.9 ms and Vector busy 139.7 -> 123.5 ms after WVIEWS, exactly the deleted work. Vector-EXCLUSIVE collapsed 27-31 -> 12.4 ms, so the bottleneck MOVED: now Tensor 15.4 / Vector 12.4 / Scalar 11.6 ms exclusive, 42.9 ms total (23.6% of span), and the step is 70% overlapped. THE BIG NEGATIVE: nkilib attention_bwd is only ~3.5 ms of EXCLUSIVE time despite 101.5 ms of instruction time - it is almost fully overlapped, so replacing it (the multi-day project I called the only remaining structural lever on 2026-09-24) would buy almost nothing. Closed for one measurement instead of days of work. REMAINING items are FRAGMENTED: mlp_bwd matmuls ~3.6 ms (v47:2024) + ~2.8 ms (2050/2057/2011); head_bwd's softcap block (s9:3463-3483) 3.2 ms Vector + 3.0 ms Scalar - a SERIAL Vector<->Scalar ping-pong, so interleaving two independent (half, chunk) blocks should overlap them (a DIFFERENT mechanism from the per-instruction-overhead interleaving refuted on 09-24); the fused layer_fwd op internals ~5 ms across three engines. Reaching 0.9700 needs ~10 ms = 3-5 separate kernel changes at ~1-3 ms each.

description: critical-path capture on the ~103 ms FORWARD graph (the half never profiled)
val_bpb: is there a second concentration like the weight-views one?
column10: The step's two big graphs are the BACKWARD (200 ms span, vector-dominated, already analysed) and the FORWARD (103 ms span, SCALAR-dominated: scalar 61% / vector 50% / dma 49% / tensor 41%). Forward exclusive time = Tensor 7.6 + Scalar 6.8 + Vector 5.1 + GpSimd 1.6 + Sync 1.1 = 22.1 ms (21.4%), plus 8.1 ms (7.8%) of PURE IDLE - no engine working - against only 2.4% idle in the backward. Top forward item: the out-projection matmul in post_attn_fwd_h (v50:1444), MATMUL 7.91 + LDWEIGHTS 1.98 ms attributed = ~4.4 ms true. Its 1:1 LDWEIGHTS:MATMUL ratio is diagnostic: it passes the ACTIVATION tile as `stationary` and the weight as `moving`, so the PE array is reloaded every tile instead of holding the weight across token tiles. Swapping the operands would help but is worth ~4.4 ms at most. Everything else is <1 ms per line. CONCLUSION: after WVIEWS there is NO remaining concentration in either graph - top items are 3-5 ms. Reaching 0.9700 (-0.0009, needs ~10 ms off the step) means 3-5 separate kernel surgeries at ~0.0002 each. The one structurally different lever left is the forward's 8.1 ms of idle, which is inter-kernel sync/launch gaps (~48 kernel launches per forward at ~0.17 ms each) - recovering it means FUSING pre_attn+attention+post_attn into fewer kernels, i.e. the megakernel direction, a multi-day build.

column10: _FMAX=256 costs -14% steps (580 vs 674) and +0.0174 bpb. Knob verified live in both logs ('chunks per 1024-token row: 2' vs '4'). So the ~100 ms of dependency-chain slack in the two graphs (backward span 199.9 vs busiest engine 139.7; forward 103.0 vs 62.8) is NOT harvestable by giving the list scheduler more independent chunks - doubling the instruction count costs far more than the extra overlap earns. _FMAX=512 is simultaneously the PSUM fp32 free-dim cap AND the optimum, i.e. a boundary optimum, so there is nothing to tune here. IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY worth keeping: DELETING 38% of all vector instructions (ROPE_WIDE) moved the step by ZERO, but DOUBLING the instruction count here costs 14%. Instruction count is not a currency you can spend, only one you can waste - the kernels are already at a scheduling sweet spot at the widest free dim the hardware allows.

description: analysis on our own calibrated measurements (no new runs)
val_bpb: is the (width, depth) plane worth reopening now that we know width>512 is blocked by OUR kernels, not the hardware?
notes: NO - THE WHOLE PLANE IS FLAT
column10: The layer stack is FLOP-PRICED IN TIME, calibrated from two clean measurements that both predict to within 1%: MLP ratio 6->8 is +16.7% layer MACs and measured +11.3% step (FLOP-proportionality predicts +11.4% with layers at 68% of the step); width 512->640 on the v9 line is +45.7% MACs and measured +30.0% step (predicts +31.1%). At 3.815 ms of step per M-MAC/token and 136 ms depth-independent, applying the -0.0132/e-fold fixed-step dense dose gives, vs 512x12 = 0.9709: 768x8 -0.0001 | 640x10 +0.0001 | 896x7 +0.0004 | 768x9 +0.0010 | 640x11 +0.0010 | 512x14 +0.0012 | 768x10 +0.0020 | 512x16 +0.0024. EVERY point is within -0.0001..+0.0024 and 512x12 is at the TOP of the plane. MECHANISM OF THE RIDGE: going UP you pay the full FLOP price (two measurements above); coming DOWN you get 0-100% refund (G_D10 on the v46 line removed 2 of 12 layers for -0.7% throughput where FLOPs predict +14%, while F_V34_D8 on an earlier line gave ~+18%). Full price up, unreliable refund down = eight measured in-stack reallocations with zero wins. ALSO CLOSED: head-count changes. Attention score FLOPs are EXACTLY invariant to head count (sum_h T*d_h = T*d), so 4x128 and 2x256 do identical MACs and the 33% attention share is a function of T/d=2 alone - this also kills GQA/MQA here (they save KV-cache and projection params, which are inference concerns). The only real width effect is per-instruction: a VectorE 128xd tile costs ~100 cycles overhead + d*128/256 of work = 0.00543 cycles/element at d=512 vs 0.00492 at d=768, i.e. 9.4% cheaper per element, worth ~4 ms of the step - correctly directed but an order of magnitude too small to carry a config. So the width>512 kernel port (28-40 h, PSUM D-chunking + an mlp_bwd SBUF restructure) should NOT be built for Phase 1.

description: ledger rows I_SYNC1b / I_SYNC4 / I_SYNC8 (no reason was ever recorded)
val_bpb: the host<->device sync cadence knob was discarded with a blank note - was that right?
column10: The numbers actually FAVOUR it: sync every 4 steps 1.120492 and every 8 steps 1.120931 against the warm reference 1.121603, i.e. -0.0011 and -0.0007. So the blank 'discard' looks wrong on the numbers and someone will re-open it. The real reason it must stay closed: record_step_boundary's contract says 'Call this exactly once per completed optimizer step, IMMEDIATELY AFTER the step (and any device synchronization) finishes', and the runner 'takes its own clock reading when each line first appears'. SYNC_EVERY>1 batches the boundary writes (the vehicle has a pending_boundaries list), so with cadence 4 boundaries 4-7 all appear at step 7 - the 5th boundary is reported LATER than the 5th step actually completed, which lengthens our excluded allowance and starts the charged budget late. That is misreporting the clock in our own favour, which is exactly the line we do not cross. The per-step synchronize(device) before record_step_boundary is therefore load-bearing and must stay. Corollary: any future 'queue the host ahead of the device' idea has the same problem and is bounded by the same rule.

description: train3_s25.py on the LOCAL RTX 4080 (torch Muon path), 1200 s budget each, paired
val_bpb: the ANVIL twin-rail Muon velocity - the missing piece of the package hypothesis
column10: BOTH ARMS RAN EXACTLY 298 STEPS, so this is step-matched with no throughput confound: rails are +0.000889 WORSE. Knob verified live: 'RAILS: twin-rail Muon velocity, fast beta 0.85 weight 0.4385, slow beta 0.98, engaging at elapsed_frac 0.4305'. Cost only 0.2% step time (dt 4.07 vs 4.06). WHY THIS MATTERED: I had hypothesised that the three ANVIL components which lost individually overnight (6-map cascade +0.00062, momentum schedule +0.00068) were FALSE NEGATIVES from testing a tuned package piece by piece - the momentum cooldown only makes sense if a slow rail carries the long-horizon signal at the end. The rails are that central piece, and they lose too, so the package story has no support left. ALL THREE ANVIL OPTIMIZER PIECES LOSE HERE; only the per-group weight-AVERAGING family transferred (v57, -0.00035 confirmed twice). Do NOT build the fused-kernel rail port (a second HBM buffer + two scalars in muon_step_stack, 4-5 h with real NaN risk) - saved. Caveats stated honestly: local GPU, a different config (EMBED_LR_SCALE 6.0, EMA 0.9933, DEVICE_BATCH 4), 298 steps with rails active for only ~170 of them, and short runs understate compounding levers. So this is a weak kill on its own - but it points the same way as the other two pieces, which is what makes it decisive. Method note: the run needed a TIME budget rather than fixed steps, because lr_multiplier and the rail engagement both key off elapsed_frac, and the standard gpu_gdn.sh setting of MAX_TRAIN_SECONDS=36000 would have left elapsed_frac near 0 - no warmdown and rails that never engage, i.e. a silent no-op experiment.

description: train3_s25.py, v55 reference env, 900 s budget, EMA_TABLES off vs on
val_bpb: can a 900 s screen tune the tail-EMA parameters? (I launched a 7-arm sweep assuming yes)
notes: NO - SWEEP INVALID, KILLED AFTER 2 ARMS
column10: EMA_TABLES=1 measures +0.000420 WORSE at 900 s, the OPPOSITE SIGN to the full gates (T_V56 0.970790 @4260 -> T_V57 0.970513 @4239 = -0.000422 better, itself confirmed by G_S20REF/G_S20TAB at -0.000289). Step counts are 2049 vs 2040, so this is a real quality difference, not throughput. CAUSE: the EMA DECAY is measured in STEPS while the EMA WINDOW is a FRACTION of the run, so halving the budget changes their ratio. At 1800 s the window is 0.15 x 4233 = 635 steps against a 1/(1-0.997) = 333-step horizon (ratio 1.9); at 900 s it is ~307 steps against the same 333 (ratio 0.9), so the average is UNDERTRAINED and blending toward it hurts. RULE: any averaging/EMA experiment must run at the FULL budget - a short screen can invert it. COROLLARY THAT SETTLED TWO KNOBS WITH NO RUNS: what matters is window/horizon, not window length. Ours is 1.9 and the ANVIL record's is 298/149.5 = 2.0, so WE ARE ALREADY AT THEIR RATIO - which also explains why the twelve earlier EMA rows in this ledger all read as a plateau, and why the 'rescale the decay to 0.998113' idea would move the ratio to 1.27, i.e. away from the optimum. The remaining free parameters are only the two BLEND coefficients, which are pure post-hoc mixing: v59 + SAVE_EMA_PARTS stores raw and averaged weights separately so experimental/blend_sweep.py can grid them EXACTLY offline on the local GPU with ZERO gate noise - the first sweep on this project not limited by the 0.00025 floor.

description: submission_v59_clean_emaparts.py, SAVE_EMA_PARTS=1 (a dev INSTRUMENT, not a candidate)
val_bpb: store the raw and averaged weights separately so the blend coefficients can be swept exactly offline

val_bpb: the first hyperparameter sweep on this project NOT limited by the 0.00025 gate-noise floor
column10: 36-point deterministic grid over (EMA_BLEND, EMA_TABLE_BLEND). The blend is applied ONCE at the end and does not affect training, so one run's raw/avg pair determines the optimum EXACTLY - a gate can only add noise to a number we can compute. Full-eval column at tables=0.65: main 0.35 -> 0.971638, 0.5 -> 0.971284, 0.65 -> 0.971163, 0.75 -> 0.971205 = a clean interior optimum at 0.65 worth -0.000475. Table blend 0.65 confirmed optimal (subset: 0.5 -> 0.981344, 0.65 -> 0.981333, 0.8 -> 0.981352). THE LEDGER'S OLD VERDICT WAS WRONG TWICE OVER: the earlier sweep (0.1/0.35/0.5, '0.35 best, 0.5 a wash') used noisy gates on an effect HALF the size of their noise floor, never tried 0.65, and predates v57 - once the token/value tables are averaged too the two groups' averages are mutually consistent and the matrix group can be leaned on harder, so fixing one thing MOVED the optimum of another. Absolute values here sit ~0.001 above the box's in-run number, which is the known local-GPU-vs-Neuron eval gap (see T36_gate, +0.0007); only within-device comparisons are used. GENERALISE THIS: any post-hoc hyperparameter can be swept exactly this way, and other 'flat plateau' verdicts in this ledger may be gate-noise artifacts.

Session total: 0.970871 (v55) -> 0.969816 (v60) = -0.001055.

val_bpb: should the four averaging groups have DIFFERENT blend coefficients, as the ANVIL record does?
column10: Coordinate descent over four independent blends, two full rounds, deterministic: per-group gain +0.000000. Every group's optimum is 0.65 and both rounds agree. matrices 0.35/0.5/0.65/0.8/0.95 -> 0.981800/0.981453/0.981333*/0.981426/0.981723 (a clear interior optimum); head 0.981353/0.981335/0.981333*/0.981347/0.981378 (nearly flat); scalars 0.981438/0.981362/0.981333*/0.981348/0.981410; tables 0.981382/0.981344/0.981333*/0.981352/0.981400. So one shared coefficient is already the joint optimum even though the group mixes 50.3M Muon matrices, a 4.19M head and 93 scalars. The record blends these separately; here it buys nothing.

val_bpb: the last untested member of the ANVIL ships family: rescale each averaged tensor to its pre-averaging Frobenius norm
notes: WORSE - AND THE PREMISE IS INVERTED HERE
column10: none 0.981333 | stacks 0.981920 | stacks+head 0.981904 | tables 0.981398 | all big tensors 0.981934. Every variant LOSES, stacks by +0.00059. MECHANISM, and it is why this does not transfer: decontraction assumes averaging SHRINKS the norm. Here the blend's norm is LARGER than the raw weights' - measured ratios ||raw||/||blend|| = 0.9822 (wte), 0.9859 (vte), 0.9854 (vte_mid), 0.9842 (vte2), 0.9986 (lm_head) - because our warmdown and weight decay shrink weights late in training, so the tail average sits at a larger norm than the final point. Forcing the norm back down undoes something useful. THE AVERAGING FAMILY IS NOW CLOSED END TO END: tables in (v57, -0.00042), blend 0.65 (v60, -0.00048), per-group refinement (zero), decay and window (already at the record's window/horizon ratio of ~2), decontraction (worse), and Richardson lag (subsumed - it is algebraically just a smaller blend, and we optimised the blend directly). We captured ~-0.0009 of the record's biggest-rated quality item and the remainder is genuinely not there for us.

val_bpb: how big is the SAME-FILE gate-to-gate spread really?
column10: Two gates of the IDENTICAL file: T_V58 0.970383 @4233 and T_V58b 0.969995 @4240. Step-adjusted to 4240 that is 0.970335 vs 0.969995 = a 0.00034 SPREAD on the same code. The project's working figure of ~0.00025 per gate is therefore optimistic, and any single-gate claim below ~0.0005 needs n>=2 per side. CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM: I reported v60's gain as -0.000484 'agreeing with the offline prediction of -0.000475 to 0.00001'. That agreement was partly luck - it used ONE control. Against the MEAN of both v58 controls (step-adjusted to 4245: 0.970300 and 0.969961, mean 0.970131) v60's 0.969816 is -0.000315. The deterministic offline figure of -0.000475 remains the better estimate of the BLEND EFFECT ITSELF, because it holds the training run fixed and only varies the post-hoc coefficient; the gate comparison adds whole-run noise on top of it. The two are consistent within ~1 sd. THIS STRENGTHENS THE OFFLINE METHOD RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT: a 0.00034 same-file spread is most of the effect size of every lever left on this project, which is exactly why post-hoc parameters should be swept deterministically instead of gated.

description: submission_v61_clean_bteema.py (EMA_TABLE_MAX raised to admit the 2^18 x 512 bigram table)
val_bpb: should the 134.2M-element bigram table be in the tail EMA too? It is 65% of all parameters and trains at the same 4.5x LR as the four tables v57 added.

Log confirms the path: 'tail-EMA table group (blend 0.65): wte, vte, vte_mid, vte2, bte(134,217,728) | excluded: ' (nothing excluded). column10: **311.6 ms of device work is queued at the moment the host leaves to fetch a batch** (mean over steps 10-39). The threshold was >100 ms = fully covered. description: submission_raw/train3_canon.py, CANON_PRE=3 (learnable width-3 causal depthwise conv on the residual stream, identity init), full gate, KILLED at step 30
val_bpb: ranked quality item 6 (Canon conv, -0.002..-0.005 at fixed steps), at the ONE placement that sits outside the fused layer op and so needs no kernel change
notes: DEAD ON THROUGHPUT - AND IT CLOSES AN ENTIRE CLASS
column10: dt 2.93 s/step vs v72's 0.424, i.e. 7x SLOWER, stable from step 2 to step 30, with NO eager fallback in the log - the compiled graph itself is that much worse. The conv is 12 torch ops (slice+cat+mask+3 mul+2 add) on the residual stream between the fused layer ops; it adds ~2.5 s. GENERAL RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: inserting ANY torch op into the residual stream between the fused layer_fwd/layer_bwd ops is unshippable on this stack. That is not specific to the conv - it also prices out MUDD-style dynamic residual mixing (the research pass's #3, -0.0019) and every other 'small op between layers' architecture idea. All remaining ARCHITECTURE work must go INSIDE the NKI kernels; the cheap remaining levers are all optimizer-side or target-side, which never touch the graph. Identity init was verified first: step-0 loss 9.0115 canon-on vs 9.0115 canon-off, bit-equal, so the wiring was correct and only the cost was fatal. Quality question therefore UNANSWERED, not answered negatively.

description: code read of MuonAdamW._muon_step in the v72 lineage, against a fresh modded-nanogpt/Track-3 research pass (46 entries, n=8-20 seeds)
val_bpb: re-run the competitive recon that quality-levers-2026-09-26 says to repeat monthly: which published mechanisms are actually missing from OUR stack?
notes: TWO OF THE TOP CANDIDATES ARE ALREADY SHIPPED - CHECK THE CODE BEFORE BUILDING
column10: NorMuon (arXiv 2510.05491, PR #276, published 3375->3300 steps ~= -0.0007 for us) is ALREADY IN _muon_step: v_mean = g.square().mean(dim=red_dim) is the per-row second moment OF THE ORTHOGONALISED update, second.lerp_(v_mean, 1-beta2) is its EMA at beta2=0.90, step_size=rsqrt, and the (v_norm / v_norm_new) factor is exactly the Frobenius renormalisation NorMuon prescribes. Cautious Weight Decay (arXiv 2510.12402, PR #328, ~-0.0002) is ALSO already there: mask=(g*w)>=0 then w.sub_(lr*g + lr*wd*w*mask) decays only the coordinates where update and weight agree in sign. STILL MISSING and worth building: EMA-Nesterov lookahead (PR #308, n=20 on plain Muon, ~-0.0018) and multi-token prediction (PR #178, ~-0.0014) - both built this session. MISSING BUT PRICED OUT: MUDD dynamic residual mixing (PR #259, -0.0084 nats at matched steps, the largest published matched-step delta found) is dead here on C_PRE3's 7x-step-time finding, because it inserts torch ops into the residual stream. MISSING, LOW VALUE: Normalized Correction (n=1), mimetic V-O init (n=7, baseline fails at p=0.11), u/w-floor (needs the NKI Muon kernel). LESSON: I described our stack to the research pass as 'Muon with Polar Express' and got back two mechanisms we already have. Describe the optimizer by reading _muon_step, not from memory.

description: re-read of runs/C_PRE3.log after the same failure mode appeared in C_MTPB
val_bpb: was the 7x step time really the cost of the residual-stream conv?
notes: NO - RETRACTS THE C_PRE3 ROW AND EVERYTHING I CONCLUDED FROM IT
column10: C_PRE3 logged TWO CAUGHT NKI lowering failures that each fall back to a slow path: 'scatter x4 unavailable ([NkiDispatch] Python lower_func failed ... ) per-table path' and 'NKI AdamW kernel unavailable (...) using the PyTorch step'. The embedding scatter and the ENTIRE optimizer therefore ran off their fused kernels for the whole run. That alone accounts for the 2.93 s vs 0.424 s, so NONE of the 7x can be attributed to the conv. RETRACTED: 'inserting any torch op into the residual stream between the fused layer ops is unshippable', and with it the pricing-out of MUDD-style dynamic residual mixing (the research pass's #3, -0.0084 nats at matched steps - the largest published matched-step delta found). The Canon conv's real cost is UNKNOWN and the quality question is still open. Note _muon_step and the AdamW path both do 'except Exception: self.use_nki = False', i.e. ONE kernel that will not lower silently disables the fused optimizer for the rest of the run and only prints one line among thousands. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME THIS PROJECT HAS CLOSED AN AXIS ON AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT (cf. the EMA cold-start bug retracting the compiler-flag/hoist/HDC verdicts, and Q_ROT's straggler zero that tested nothing). Rule: before believing ANY step-time regression, grep the log for 'unavailable' and 'falling back'.

description: train3_canon.py MTP_W1=0.5 MTP_W2=0.25 (multi-token prediction as stochastic target replacement), full 1800 s, scored OFFLINE
val_bpb: ranked research item #2 (modded-nanogpt PR #178, record 52->53, ~-0.0014 expected)
column10: Scored offline on the local GPU against ckpt/v72_final.pt with IDENTICAL tokens/code/device: v72 0.968900, MTP 0.974043, delta +0.005144. MTP also ran +0.7%% MORE steps (~4420 vs 4390, dt 0.40 vs 0.410 s), so the quality cost is ~+0.0053 - about 20x the gate-noise floor and equivalent to LOSING 16%% of steps. MECHANISM for why it does not transfer: the published rationale is that early training is learning the n-gram distribution and MTP is a cheap proxy for a bigger batch - but this model ALREADY has a dedicated 2^18 x 512 hashed BIGRAM table (134.2M params, 65%% of all parameters) doing exactly that job, so the aux targets add conflicting gradient without adding information we lack. Predicting 2-3 tokens ahead at vocab 8192 (short tokens) is also much harder than at GPT-2 vocab. CAVEAT KEPT: this tested the STOCHASTIC form (one target per token, drawn with prob w_k/sum w), which adds gradient variance the exact weighted-CE sum does not; 43%% of targets were replaced. Exact MTP would need head-kernel surgery and is NOT worth it against a +0.005 prior. The in-run eval CRASHED in prepare.causality_check (NkiDispatch lowering failure at the 4-row eval shape) with the checkpoint already saved - which is how this was scored at all. METHOD: scoring saved checkpoints offline is strictly better than comparing two gates in-run, because it removes the eval-subset difference AND the eval crash; v72 reproduced to all six digits.

val_bpb: EMA-Nesterov lookahead (PR #308, n=20 isolated on plain Muon, ~-0.0018): what does the wrapper cost?
notes: UNSHIPPABLE AS EAGER OPS - AND NOT WORTH THE KERNEL WORK
column10: 4.94 s/step against 0.40 for the same file with the knob off, and ZERO NKI fallbacks, so the cost is genuinely the wrapper. It is ~72 eager elementwise ops over the owned shards; 4.54 s / 72 = 63 ms PER EAGER OP, which calibrates something broadly useful: an eager elementwise op on this device costs ~60-75 ms almost regardless of size, ~100x the fused path, and 550 MB of bandwidth would be ~5 ms - so it is pure per-dispatch overhead, not traffic. That also retro-explains why the vehicle has fused NKI kernels for Muon/AdamW at all, and why my MTP target remap cost +226 ms/step until it moved to the host. NOT BUILDING IT IN-KERNEL, for a reason rather than for cost: the wrapper shifts weights along an EMA of past updates at gamma=0.99, i.e. a ~100-step horizon of STALE state, and this project has established the opposite mechanism across six results - shorter horizons win here because the warmdown makes late weights improve fast, so any mechanism averaging older state pays a bias cost exceeding its variance benefit (it predicted v68 correctly, and it is why all three ANVIL momentum pieces lost). The research pass also notes the same wrapper bought only -40 steps (~-0.0004) on a heavily-stacked baseline, and ours is heavily stacked (NorMuon and cautious weight decay are already in _muon_step). Expected value therefore ~0 to negative against 2-4 h of NKI work on two kernels. Revisit only if the in-house horizon mechanism is ever refuted.

description: train3_canon.py LOADER_CPU=1 (bit-identical math, train loader built on the host), full 1800 s, scored offline
val_bpb: is the +2%% steps seen in the MTP arm a free throughput win from moving the loader to the host?
notes: INVALID - 2779 NKI FALLBACKS - AND IT YIELDS A NEW INVALIDATION RULE
column10: The run took 2779 silent fallbacks (scatter x4 -> per-table path, NKI AdamW -> PyTorch step) and ran at 0.64 s/step for 2770 steps, so it says NOTHING about the loader question - which is still open. What it DOES say is more useful: scored offline it is 1.028778 vs v72's 0.968900, i.e. +0.059878, but the step deficit is only ln(4390/2770) = 0.4605 e-fold which at the established -0.0293/e-fold predicts just +0.0135. **+0.046 is therefore UNEXPLAINED by step count**, so a run that falls back is not merely slower, its QUALITY is damaged - most likely the per-table scatter or the PyTorch AdamW path is not numerically equivalent to the fused kernel it replaces (both are years-old code paths nothing exercises). RULE: a run with ANY fallbacks is invalid in BOTH speed and quality; check the NKI_FALLBACKS line before reading any bpb. Deliberately NOT updating the exchange rate from this point - it is one confounded observation, and the clean same-file measurement (C_2400 vs v55, -0.0293) stands. CAUSE OF THE FALLBACKS, from six arms: every arm launched after a run that CRASHED took them (C_LDCPU 2779, C_MTP 127, C_PRE3 40), every arm launched after a clean finish took zero (C_MTPB, C_MTPS, C_NESTS), and six v72/v71/v70 gates have zero. Mitigation now in place: EVAL_PUBLIC=0 on every arm so runs finish cleanly (the in-run causality_check is what crashes), plus clearing /tmp/nki_* before relaunching.

description: train3_canon.py CANON_PRE=3, CLEAN state (/tmp/nki_* cleared, 0 fallbacks, conv verified live by num_params +18,432)
val_bpb: re-test the Canon residual conv after C_PRE3's 7x was attributed to silent kernel fallbacks
notes: CONV REALLY IS THAT EXPENSIVE - THE RETRACTION IS ITSELF PARTLY WITHDRAWN
column10: 2.68 s/step against v72's 0.41 with **ZERO fallbacks**, stable over steps 20-40. So of C_PRE3's 2.5 s excess the fallbacks were only ~0.25 s and the CONV ITSELF costs ~2.27 s. The original C_PRE3 conclusion therefore SURVIVES a clean re-test, and MUDD-style dynamic residual mixing is priced out again. The retraction was still procedurally correct - that measurement WAS confounded and could not support the claim - it just happens the confound was small. Net lesson unchanged: check for fallbacks; but ALSO re-measure rather than assume a confound was the whole story. MECHANISM: 2.27 s / 24 conv applications (12 layers x fwd+bwd) = ~95 ms each, which is the ~60-75 ms-per-EAGER-op figure, so these ops are NOT being fused into the compiled graph - a torch op placed between the fused layer custom-ops apparently does not get folded into the graph on this backend. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the conv inside layer_fwd would be nearly free (the kernel already holds the data in SBUF), so the question worth answering is whether it helps AT FIXED STEPS - and that belongs on the local GPU, not here, where 2.68 s/step makes a full gate worthless.

val_bpb: adversarial code review found a train/eval RMSNorm epsilon mismatch: kernels use finfo(bf16).eps = 0.0078125, the scored head_logits uses F.rms_norm with NO eps and x is fp32-typed so it gets 1.19e-7. 65,000x apart. Does it matter?
notes: REAL BUT TINY: -0.000065, FREE, BANK IT
column10: Measured mean(x^2) at the head = 77.37 (dtype fp32, confirming the promotion: bigram_lambda is an fp32 Parameter so the residual stream stays fp32-typed). Relative logit-scale error = eps/(2*mean x^2) = 0.005%%, so the effect is small BY MECHANISM, not by luck. Exact bpb: scorer default 0.968900, training's bf16 eps 0.968835 = **-0.000065**. Below one gate's noise but EXACTLY measured offline and deterministic, so it counts. FIX is one line and changes NO training math: make module-level norm() use eps=0.0078125. On Neuron, training goes through the layer ops and head_fwd (both already bf16 eps) and never calls norm(), so the change touches only the eval path and the torch fallbacks - which also makes the fallbacks consistent with the kernels, and the module docstring's 'the two are the same function of the same weights' finally true. NOTE the existing check_fused_loss CANNOT detect this: it runs at step 0 where both output projections are zero-init, so mean(x^2) ~ 75 makes the eps term 5e-5 relative and invisible. BANKED for the next version bundle - not worth a v## on its own.

description: train3_canon.py ROPE_FRAC 0.5 -> 0.25, full 1800 s, 0 fallbacks, scored offline against v72
val_bpb: ROPE_FRAC has only ever been run at 0.5 in 634 ledger rows - it was introduced BUNDLED with KEY_OFFSET (the pair was -0.0032) and never swept. Free arm: it only changes host-side rotary tables, no recompile.
notes: MUCH WORSE +0.0213 - but the axis is SENSITIVE, which is the useful part
column10: 4410 steps (vs v72 4390, so slightly MORE steps) and 0 fallbacks, so this is a pure quality loss of ~+0.0214 - two orders of magnitude above the noise floor. ROPE_FRAC is therefore NOT on a plateau like every other swept scalar: it has real curvature and 0.5 is strongly better than 0.25. Mechanism: inv_freq[64*RF:] = 0, so RF=0.25 leaves only the top 16 of 64 frequency pairs rotating and makes head dims 16:64 and 80:128 positional-free - the model loses most of its relative-position resolution. C_RF75 (the upward direction) is the arm that matters; if it is also worse, 0.5 is a genuine interior optimum and the axis closes. **COUPLING NOBODY HAD NOTICED, and it constrains three arms:** KEY_OFFSET shifts head dims hq:2hq, and the stationary (non-rotating) dims are [64*RF,64) u [64+64*RF,128). Keeping the shift inside the stationary block requires hq >= 64*RF AND hq <= 32, so at RF=0.5 **hq = HD//4 = 32 is the ONLY consistent value** - KEY_OFFSET_DIV is not an independent knob at all. C_KO2 (hq=64) and C_KO8 (hq=16) would both shift ROTATING dims and were dropped from the queue; the consistent dose test moves both knobs together (C_RF25K8 = RF 0.25 + DIV 8). Note C_RF75 is itself mildly confounded for the same reason: at RF=0.75 the stationary block is only 48:64, so hq=32 shifts rotating dims 32:48.

description: train3_canon.py ROPE_FRAC 0.75 and 0.25, full 1800 s, 0 fallbacks each, both scored offline against v72
val_bpb: sweep the one architecture constant that 635 ledger rows only ever ran at a single value
notes: AXIS CLOSED - 0.5 IS A MEASURED INTERIOR OPTIMUM
column10: Dose curve, all offline-exact against v72 0.968900: RF 0.25 -> +0.021334 (4410 steps, i.e. MORE steps, so pure quality), RF 0.50 -> 0 (ours), RF 0.75 -> +0.001940 at 4330 steps which is -1.4%% steps worth +0.0004, so ~+0.0015 quality-adjusted. So 0.5 is a genuine INTERIOR optimum and the axis is closed in both directions. The curve is strongly ASYMMETRIC - going down (fewer rotating frequency pairs, less relative-position resolution) is ~14x worse than going up - which says the model wants MORE positional resolution and 0.5 is a compromise forced by KEY_OFFSET needing stationary dims to shift. PARTIAL CORRECTION to my own coupling argument: I predicted RF>0.5 is 'architecturally inconsistent' because hq:2hq then overlaps rotating dims, and it IS worse - but only by 0.0015, not catastrophically, so the RoPE/KEY_OFFSET coupling is real yet mild. Do not use it to dismiss arms outright; C_KO2/C_KO8 were dropped on that reasoning and that was probably over-strict, though they remain low-value. WHAT THIS EXPOSES: the RF=0.5 + KEY_OFFSET package was measured as a PAIR at v24 (-0.0032 vs RF=1.0/no-KO) and never separated since, across ~48 versions. The new dose curve is consistent with the pair still being right, but KEY_OFFSET's own contribution at the CURRENT config has never been measured - queued as C_KO0.

description: prepare.py eval-public on an arm checkpoint without the arm's env vars
val_bpb: how do you score a knob arm's checkpoint correctly?
notes: RULE: ALWAYS PASS THE ARM'S FULL ENV TO ITS SCORING JOB
column10: S_CANQ died with 'Unexpected key(s) in state_dict: transformer.h.N.canon_p' because load_for_eval rebuilds the model from the VEHICLE at its env defaults and then load_state_dict(strict=True). That failure is the SAFE case - it is loud. The DANGEROUS case is a knob that changes the forward WITHOUT changing the parameter set: VE_T1/VE_T2 (same three value-embedding tables, different layer assignment) and KEY_OFFSET=0 (no doc_start, different kernel) both load CLEANLY and would produce a SILENTLY WRONG score, because the scored model is not the model that trained. Knobs that are safe without their env: ROPE_FRAC and ROPE_BASE (the cos/sin tables are buffers, so the CHECKPOINT's tables are restored after init_weights), SOFTCAP and SINK_INIT (inits of learned parameters, so the trained values are restored), and NS_STEPS / GLOBAL_LR / PREFIX_AUX / MTP / LOADER_CPU (training-only, no eval effect). Because the dangerous set is silent, the rule is unconditional: every scoring job carries the same NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_* env as the arm that produced the checkpoint. The JOB line format supports it - trn2_job.sh runs the command through bash -c, so a VAR=val prefix works.

description: train3_canon.py CANON_PRE=3 vs off, FRAC_BY_STEPS=1 NUM_STEPS=600, both exactly 600 steps, 0 fallbacks each, scored on the box with the official scorer
val_bpb: does the Canon residual conv help AT ALL? Its 2.68 s/step as torch ops makes a time-budgeted gate worthless, but inside layer_fwd it would be nearly free, so the only decision-relevant question is the fixed-step quality delta.
notes: BIGGEST RESULT OF THE SESSION: -0.013664 AT FIXED STEPS
column10: Learnable width-3 causal depthwise conv on the residual stream at the block input, identity-init (tap0=1, rest 0), document-start masked, 12 layers x 3 taps x 512 = 18,432 new params in a flat AdamW group. At a matched 600 steps with an identical LR curve (FRAC_BY_STEPS makes the warmdown follow step fraction, verified: lrm 0.474 at step 350/600): canon 1.1077839 vs baseline 1.1214480 = **-0.013664**, which is ~4x the remaining gap to 9th place. THREE CAVEATS, all real: (1) 600 steps is far from the 4390-step operating point and the model is at 1.12 bpb vs 0.968 there, so the gain may DECAY - and this project has a precedent for exactly that failure mode, since MTP's whole rationale was early n-gram learning and the 134M bigram table already covers it at convergence. A 1200-step pair is queued to get the TREND rather than a second point. (2) The 600-step screen NOISE FLOOR is unmeasured; C_REFQ2 repeats the baseline screen to establish it, though -0.0137 is far above any plausible screen noise. (3) The value is entirely contingent on an IN-KERNEL implementation: as torch ops the conv costs 2.68 s/step against 0.41, which at fixed time would lose ~+0.055. Inside layer_fwd the tile is already in SBUF and the kernel already does a cross-tile carry for KEY_OFFSET, so the machinery exists; estimate 1-2 days for fwd+bwd plus the weight gradient.

description: q12 died at 06:43:38 on 'GATE BLOCKED: a training run holds the device (refusing S_V72REF)'
val_bpb: why did the queue stop after only one scoring job?
column10: trn2_job.sh gates on pgrep -f "[s]ubmission_v[0-9]*_.*\.py", and my JOB command contained 'submission_raw/submission_v72_clean_dyfuse.py', so the gate matched the RUNNER'S OWN command line and refused the job. A refused JOB then hits 'exit 1' in trn2_queue.sh and kills the ENTIRE queue, leaving the box idle. This trap is already recorded in the session summary and I still hit it. FIX: never put a filename matching submission_v[0-9]*_.*\.py in a JOB command. Use submission_raw/train3_canon.py as --train-py for every checkpoint instead - with all knobs off it is mathematically identical to v72 and has the same parameter set, so a strict state_dict load works. SECOND-ORDER LESSON: a refused JOB should not be fatal to the queue; the runner's exit-1-on-refusal is right for a launch race but wrong for a self-block. Watch for idle-box gaps after any JOB entry.

description: train3_canon.py GLOBAL_LR=1.15 and 0.87 (ALL four learning rates scaled jointly via _BATCH_LR), full 1800 s, 0 fallbacks, scored on the box against S_V72BOX
val_bpb: every LR was swept ONE AT A TIME and each sits on a plateau - but the JOINT direction was never tested, and all four were tuned when the run was 25%% shorter
notes: NO GAIN, AXIS ASYMMETRIC - flat below, cliff above
column10: Box-side baseline S_V72BOX (v72 checkpoint, single-core official scorer, 2,097,152 tokens) = **0.9692435**. Joint LR x0.87 -> 0.9694052 = **+0.00016**, i.e. flat. Joint LR x1.15 -> 0.9717189 = **+0.0025**, clearly worse. So the joint direction gains nothing, but the shape is informative: the surface is FLAT on the low side and a CLIFF on the high side, which says the current point is not over-tuned and there is no headroom from scaling everything up. Trying 0.75 is safe but unlikely to pay. NOTE the box-side single-rank eval reads ~+0.0011 higher than the 8-rank in-run eval (0.9692435 vs the 0.968089/0.968186 gates) because world_size=1 draws a different eval subset - only ever compare box-side to box-side.

description: trn2_job.sh + trn2_queue.sh + trn2_run.sh all gate on pgrep -f "native_venv/bin/[p]ython"
val_bpb: why did an 87 s scoring job get declared finished after 20 s?
notes: INFRA RACE - FIXED BY USING THE FULL PATH TO PYTHON IN JOB COMMANDS
column10: trn2_job.sh runs its command as: bash -c 'source .../native_venv/bin/activate && <cmd>'. A venv-activated 'python foo.py' has the command line 'python foo.py' - it does NOT contain 'native_venv/bin/python'. That string is the pattern used by (a) trn2_queue.sh's job-wait loop, (b) trn2_queue.sh's free() device check, and (c) trn2_run.sh's HARD LAUNCH GATE. Consequence: the queue declared S_V72BOX finished 20 s into an 87 s eval, and the gates would have launched an 8-way TRAINING RUN on top of a live eval. S_V72BOX happened to survive and produce 0.9692435, but this is a silent-corruption race, not a cosmetic bug: a training run launching mid-eval would produce a plausible wrong number. FIX: every JOB command now invokes /home/ubuntu/workspace/native_venv/bin/python explicitly so all three gates can see it. This is the SECOND gate-pattern bug today - the first was pgrep matching the ssh command's own command line (fixed with a self-escaping [c]lass pattern).

description: submission_raw/train3_b1.py, train3_b2.py, train3_b3.py - three coordinated multi-change branches from three Opus agents, each entirely behind one env flag with flag-off verified identical to baseline
val_bpb: escape the local optimum by a coordinated JUMP rather than single-knob perturbation, screened at 600 fixed steps against the 1.121448 baseline
notes: ALL THREE QUEUED - each ships its own falsifier, which is the useful part
column10: B1 CAPACITY REALLOCATION: thesis is that RANK SHOULD FOLLOW VISITS-PER-ROW. The 2^18 x 512 bigram table gives 262k rows 512 free params each but a typical row is visited only a few hundred times per screen, while the 8192-row token tables get ~10k visits each. Proposes 2^19 x 128 x 2 reads + one shared 512x256 projection fitted from all 78M visits, halving the table 134M -> 67M, with scale-preserving init so EMBEDDING_LR needs no change (a derivation, not a guess). Supports it from OUR OWN rows: 2^17->2^18 won (-0.0023) but 2^18->2^19 LOST (+0.0009), which is the signature of rows too wide to train rather than running out of addresses; and BIGRAM_SPLIT=2 at constant params was a wash, i.e. flat along exactly this axis. Predicts -0.002 (band -0.008..+0.005). DELIBERATELY does NOT respend the freed params in the body, because every dense direction there is measured non-positive at fixed time. Its FALSIFIER is one knob (B1_RANK=256 B1_ROWS=18 B1_READS=1, a pure width halving at baseline addressing): if that loses by >0.001, per-row width is load-bearing and the WHOLE reallocation axis is dead - running that FIRST instead of the package. B2 OPTIMIZATION REGIME: argues lr and wd are ONE knob, because Muon's fixed-Frobenius update makes ||W|| equilibrate at sqrt(lr/wd) and every matrix is read through a norm, so the forward only sees temperature T=lr/||W||. Converts our MATRIX_LR curve into T coordinates and PREDICTS OUR WEIGHT-DECAY ROWS OUT OF SAMPLE (wd 0.20 predicted +0.0042 vs measured +0.0032/+0.0045; wd 0.05 predicted +0.0016 vs measured +0.0022/+0.0003). Jump: make wd track lrm so geometry stops moving and T becomes LINEAR rather than sqrt-compressed, spreading the anneal over the whole run instead of the last 25%%; plus terminal LR 0.02->0.034, warmup 50->35, Muon momentum peak 0.95->0.97, NorMuon beta2 0.90->0.93, EMA window 0.75->0.60 at decay 0.9982. Predicts -0.0025 full length and states the 600-step screen UNDER-expresses by ~+0.0007, so it gets a FULL GATE not a screen. Its falsifier is a NORM DIAGNOSTIC that tests the reasoning rather than the score: baseline Muon norms should fall ~1.7x across the warmdown, B2's stay flat - folded into C_REF12 for free. B3 TOWER MIXTURE: connects two of our own numbers nobody had put together - output-space ensembling of two models is -0.020 (our largest single quality figure) while depth is nearly free (7-16 within +0.0024) - so buy diversity with DEPTH instead of time: two parallel 6-layer towers over the same 12 blocks sharing the tables, own head and softcap each, mixture of their output distributions, different RoPE frac and value-embedding order per tower for free decorrelation. Also lifts the rank-512 softmax bottleneck (mixture-of-softmaxes) at vocab 8192, and is effectively router-free MoE so neither of the two things that killed MoE applies. Arithmetic: needs mixing gain >~0.017 to beat a ~+0.014 depth penalty plus ~+0.003 step cost. MY PRIOR IS THAT IT LOSES, because the -0.020 came from two INDEPENDENTLY TRAINED full-depth models whose errors decorrelate strongly, while these share 73%% of params and train jointly. Running it anyway FOR THE DIAGNOSTIC: one run prints each tower's bpb alone AND the mixture's, separating MIXING GAIN from DEPTH PENALTY, and those two numbers decide whether to escalate to the author's own better idea - several softmax components over ONE deep trunk, which gets the rank lifting with NO depth penalty but needs new kernel code.

notes: NO - BOTH ROPE_FRAC SCORES ARE INVALID, RE-SCORING
column10: The rotary tables are NON-PERSISTENT buffers, so they are NOT saved in the checkpoint - they are rebuilt from ROPE_FRAC/ROPE_BASE when load_for_eval constructs the model. I scored C_RF25 and C_RF75 on the local GPU with experimental/score_ckpt.py, which imports the vehicle at DEFAULT env, so both checkpoints were evaluated with ROPE_FRAC=0.5 tables while having been TRAINED at 0.25 and 0.75. That is a train/eval mismatch in the MEASUREMENT, and it inflates both numbers by an unknown amount - a model trained with dims 16:64 stationary was scored with only 32:64 stationary. RETRACTED: the dose curve (+0.0213 / +0.0015), the claim that 0.5 is a measured INTERIOR OPTIMUM, and 'the axis is closed'. The KEY_OFFSET coupling argument (hq >= 64*RF and hq <= 32, so RF=0.5 forces hq=32) is UNAFFECTED because it is algebra, not measurement - but it no longer has a measurement behind the choice of 0.5. WORSE, I explicitly classified ROPE_FRAC and ROPE_BASE as SAFE-without-env in the scoring-trap row (2026-09-27T06:10) on the reasoning that 'the cos/sin tables are buffers, so the CHECKPOINT's tables are restored after init_weights'. That reasoning was wrong because I did not check whether those buffers were persistent. CORRECTED SAFE LIST: only knobs whose values are LEARNED PARAMETERS (LOGIT_SOFTCAP, SINK_INIT - both nn.Parameters in the state dict) or that are training-only (NS_STEPS, GLOBAL_LR, PREFIX_AUX, MTP, LOADER_CPU) are safe without env. Everything that shapes a BUFFER or the forward structure - ROPE_FRAC, ROPE_BASE, VE_T1/VE_T2, KEY_OFFSET, CANON_PRE, B1/B2/B3 - must carry its env into the scoring job. RULE SIMPLIFIED TO: always pass the arm's full env, no exceptions, and never reason about which are safe.

val_bpb: get the TREND of the canon gain by adding a 1200-step point to the 600-step one
notes: INVALID AS A TREND POINT - WALL_CAP_SECONDS SILENTLY TRUNCATED IT MID-WARMDOWN
column10: WALL_CAP_SECONDS defaults to 2900 and is a TOTAL-WALL guard, not a training-time guard, so it counts the ~600 s cold compile too. At 2.70 s/step that left room for only 973 of the 1200 steps. The damage is worse than a short run: FRAC_BY_STEPS derives the LR schedule from step/NUM_STEPS, so the run stopped at elapsed_frac 0.81 with **lrm still 0.229** - it never received its final anneal, while the fast reference arm completes all 1200 steps and anneals to 0.02. So the pair is neither step-matched NOR schedule-matched and cannot be compared in either direction. GENERAL HAZARD: any fixed-step run slower than about (2900 - compile)/NUM_STEPS seconds per step is silently truncated mid-schedule, and nothing in the log says 'truncated' - you have to notice num_steps < NUM_STEPS and a final lrm far above FINAL_LR_FRAC. At 2.70 s/step the safe ceiling is ~850 steps; raise it with NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_WALL_CAP_SECONDS. The 600-step pair is UNAFFECTED (both arms completed 600 steps and annealed fully), so the -0.013664 result stands. DEPRIORITISED rather than re-run: a working in-kernel conv would let me measure transfer directly with a FULL 1800 s gate, which answers the question better than any fixed-step extrapolation, so the 1200-step point is only a hedge against the kernel build failing.
